title: CyberThreat Mesh

basics.tagline: Autonomous AI red-teaming, attack surface & containment

listing.shortDescription: A 20-screen interactive security SaaS that renders a cloud attack surface as a living SVG attack graph — agent control, vulnerability feeds, temporal replay, compliance briefs, RBAC and audit trails.
listing.fullDescription: CyberThreat Mesh is a 20-page interactive SaaS-style application for visualizing and reasoning about cloud attack surfaces. It renders a cloud estate (AWS IAM roles, EC2 instances, S3 buckets, Kubernetes pods, RDS databases, Azure AD service principals) as an interactive SVG attack graph, alongside operational screens: autonomous agent control panels, vulnerability feeds, blast-radius analytics, temporal replay, compliance report generation, RBAC governance, integration health, and audit trails. The engineering center of gravity is a front-end architecture problem — how to make a data-dense, graph-heavy security product feel instant, theme-correct, and navigable across 20 screens — answered with a dual-theme design-token system, a deterministic SVG graph engine guaranteeing ≥146px minimum node spacing with curved bezier edges, a strict layout architecture (sticky header / fixed collapsible sidebar / isolated scroll viewport), a motion budget of ≤150ms on all 70+ animations calls and theme-aware chart rendering using CSS variables so every Recharts visualization adapts to the active theme without re-rendering.

cover.imageAlt: Abstract security mesh diagram with cloud assets flowing into an attack graph engine and out to alert triage

features.title: Interactive SVG attack graph
features.description: Every cloud asset is a node, every IAM trust, network route and data flow an edge — with risk status encoded by color, glow and label.

features.title: Guaranteed node spacing
features.description: A deterministic seeded grid layout guarantees ≥146px minimum node distance (spec ≥140px) while still looking organic.

features.title: Curved bezier edges
features.description: Quadratic bezier paths with a 26px perpendicular bend keep parallel edges separate from labels.

features.title: Dual-theme engine
features.description: Class-based dark mode with the same risk color tokens WCAG-compliant in both tactical dark and high-contrast light themes.

features.title: Theme-aware charts
features.description: 20+ Recharts visualizations reference CSS variables, so charts re-color on theme switch without a re-render.

features.title: Node inspector
features.description: A 150ms Framer Motion drawer shows CVSS, exploitability, edge count, MITRE techniques and tags for any node.

features.title: Agent control panels
features.description: Four autonomous agent cards with workload gauges, token counters, latency stats and thought-process execution trees.

features.title: Temporal replay
features.description: A scrubber replays T-30 → T-0; the visible graph is re-sliced from the node and edge datasets per interval.

features.title: Investigation workspace
features.description: BFS-based 2-hop sub-graph extraction around any selectable node with lateral chain forensics.

features.title: Compliance brief generator
features.description: Framework selector (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / MITRE / custom) toggles a generated readiness brief with gauges and coverage charts.

features.title: Vulnerability feed
features.description: A 35-day exploit heatmap generated deterministically from a seeded PRNG, with CVE backlog cards and threat-intel news.

features.title: Pricing calculator
features.description: Three live sliders (instances, IAM identities, simulations) recompute a monthly subscription estimate and savings donut.

challenge.summary: Security products that visualize attack graphs and threat telemetry share a recurring failure pattern: they are visually dense, slow to render, and hard to navigate. The project set out to fix the five pain points that typically make these products unusable for triage.

points.title: Cluttered graph canvases
points.description: Naive graph layouts overlap nodes, let edge lines collide with labels, and require constant pan/zoom to read — unusable for triage.

points.title: Theme-split visual language
points.description: Many dashboards force a dark theme or bolt on a light one with washed-out neon colors that fail WCAG contrast on light backgrounds.

points.title: Z-index and scroll architecture failures
points.description: Fixed sidebars that overlap sticky headers, or headers that scroll away, are common layout defects in dashboard UIs.

points.title: Skeleton-slow perceived performance
points.description: Long animation delays and blocking loading states make data-dense dashboards feel sluggish even when data is local.

points.title: 20-screen scope
points.description: A product with this many distinct workflows needs a reusable component and design system or implementation cost multiplies per screen.

solution.summary: We built a single page product shell: a living attack graph where risk is encoded by color, glow and label, operational screens built from the same dataset, and a dual-theme design system so the same product works in tactical dark mode and high-contrast light mode without layout changes.

points.title: Deterministic graph layout
points.description: A seeded mulberry32 PRNG on a 3-column grid (170px cells, ±12px jitter) guarantees ≥146px node separation by construction — provable, and identical on server and client.

points.title: Bezier edge separation
points.description: Quadratic Q-bezier paths with a 26px perpendicular bend keep parallel edges apart from labels, which render as bordered pills offset alternately top and bottom.

points.title: CSS-variable risk tokens
points.description: Deep WCAG risk colors in light mode (#9F1239 critical, #B45309 high, #0369A1 medium, #065F46 low) and neon equivalents in dark mode, derived via color-mix() for badges and borders.

points.title: Z-index-disciplined layout
points.description: Sticky header at z-40, fixed sidebar at z-30 below it (top-16, h-[calc(100vh-4rem)]), and an isolated main scroll viewport — no overlap, no scroll-away.

points.title: 150ms motion budget
points.description: All 70+ Framer Motion calls capped at ≤0.15s with ease-out easing; no blocking skeletons, panels render instantly.

points.title: One graph engine, five screens
points.description: The attack graph component powers the landing hero, public explorer, main canvas, temporal timeline, and investigation workspace — parameterized with filters, highlights and dimming.

points.title: Typed simulated data layer
points.description: UI code written against real contracts from lib/types.ts; mockData.ts implements them (~120+ records), so a live API swap later is a data-module replacement.

points.title: Theme-aware charts via CSS vars
points.description: Recharts SVG attributes reference var(--risk-*) tokens — every chart flips theme-correct with zero re-render logic.

objectives: Implement 20 fully populated product screens across four navigation categories
Ship a dual-theme engine where the same risk color tokens are WCAG-compliant in both themes
Build a reusable SVG attack graph with guaranteed minimum node spacing (spec ≥140px, implemented ≥146px)
Enforce a strict layout architecture: sticky header, fixed sidebar, isolated scrolling viewport
Cap every animation at ≤0.15s with ease-out easing and eliminate skeleton blocking
Make every chart, filter, slider and scrubber genuinely interactive against the dataset
Verify clean lint, passing production build, and all routes serving HTTP 200
Design a typed data layer that can absorb a live backend later without structural changes

closing.clientOverview: The brief asked for a complete, navigable security-product surface: a 20-screen application that demonstrates what an autonomous AI red-teaming platform looks like — attack surface mapping, blast radius analytics, agent control, and governance — implemented with honest front-end engineering. The product context is enterprise cloud security operations: SOC analysts, threat hunters, cloud security architects, and GRC auditors triage identities, workloads, and data stores continuously, and time-to-visualization plus clarity of the attack graph are core differentiators.
closing.conclusion: CyberThreat Mesh delivers a complete 20-screen, dual-themed, statically generated security-product UI. Its durable engineering value: a reusable deterministic SVG attack-graph engine with a provable minimum-spacing guarantee, a CSS-variable design-token system that keeps risk semantics correct in light and dark themes, a z-index-disciplined layout architecture with isolated scroll, a 150ms motion budget across 70+ animations, and a typed simulated data layer that stands in for a future backend. The build is green, lint is clean, and every route was verified serving HTTP 200. Everything inside is implemented; everything the product represents — AI agents, telemetry, integrations, governance — is a labeled simulation of what such a product would show.
